title: Modula-9: a language for code that must be believed
excerpt: A Wirth-family language for scientific computing and for code an AI agent writes and a person is answerable for.
content_html:
M9 is a Wirth-family language that is readable like a bank statement and checked like Rust. Every rule exists because of a real bug, and the compiler refuses that bug instead of letting the program run on and quietly produce a wrong number.

The compiler is tested on every build to make sure this program never compiles. Run it in your browser, no installation needed.

For results you have to reproduce

Every number type names its width, and nothing converts on its own. A wrong conversion stops the program instead of slipping a bad value into your mean. The tutorial goes from first steps to a real ICOS CO2 series read through zarr, a NetCDF file, regressions, and threads.

Start the tutorial

For code an AI agent writes

Types, failure modes, effects, and thread safety are stated in definition modules, and the compiler checks them all. Checks can't be turned off. M9 was itself written by an agent under review, and its claims are checked the same way.

Read the report

Measured, not claimed

  • Runtime checks cost about 3%, and can't be switched offBenchmarks
  • Mandelbrot runs as fast as C, from a 26 KB executableMethod
  • The compiler compiles itself to byte-identical outputBootstrap
  • The zarr reader matches numpy to the last digitChapter 8
  • Each language feature cites the bug it makes uncompilableThe report

Install

Linux: packages for Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, Rocky, and Arch, or build from source with only gcc.

./build.sh

macOS on Apple silicon, experimental.

brew tap atverm/m9
brew install m9

Windows 10 and 11, experimental: a zip with its own gcc and one installer. All releases
